description:
README and the landing page have diverged on brand messaging. The page was rewritten across 2026-09-20/21 (T-063); the README still speaks the old vocabulary. Raised by the founder 2026-09-21.

## Divergences, with line numbers

**1. "memory" is disclaimed on the page but is the README's headline.**
`README.md:3` — "The memory and reflection layer for people who work with AI."
The landing page's superpower callout explicitly says the opposite: "Not that Zug remembers your conversations. Transcripts are cheap and nobody wants to reread them." Memory was deliberately burned as a word during the noun search (T-063 9c) because it invites the transcript reading.

**2. "cognitive fingerprint" was retired.** The artifact noun is **persona** (T-063 9f). Eight occurrences: lines 9, 24, 39, 87, 116, 136, 154, 201, 213. Note `PERSONA.md:201` describes itself as "Cognitive fingerprint", which is now circular.

**3. Positioning.** The page opens on the problem ("You explain yourself to the same AI every single session") and defines Zug by its slot in the stack ("You configured the agent. Zug gets to know you."). The README opens on a category label. The page's framing is the newer and better-tested one.

**4. Em dashes.** The page banned them and enforces it with a test over the content object. The README is full of them. Decide whether the ban is house style or page-only. If house style, the README needs a pass.

## Worth keeping, do not lose in the rewrite

The founder flagged these explicitly.

- **The havruta line**, `README.md:9`: "Built around the Jewish concept of *havruta*: learning alongside a partner produces something neither could reach alone." This is the best statement of the thesis anywhere in the repo and the landing page does not currently make it. T-063 item 8 is the section that wants it.
- **"No database. Plain files you can read, back up, or delete."** (`:213`) Sharper than the page's equivalent.
- **The Agent Support table** (`:26-35`). It is *more honest than the landing page was*: it already uses tiers ("First-class" / "Best-effort") and already says other agents "lack the automatic session gate behavior". The page only caught up on 2026-09-21.
- **The data directory tree** (`:197-211`). Concrete, checkable, exactly the register the page aims for.

## The capability matrix should live here

`README.md:26-35` is the natural single source. The landing page spec block should be generated from it rather than hand-copied, because hand-copied facts in this repo have now gone stale twice: `app/layout.tsx` title and `app/opengraph-image.tsx` alt both shipped abandoned headlines until they were made to derive from `content.hero`.

The table needs updating regardless, per T-065: it lists three clients, and the real surface count is at least seven (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor IDE, cursor-agent CLI, Grok CLI, Antigravity, Devin CLI, Windsurf).

It also needs the read/write split that T-065 uncovered. The current note says other agents "lack the automatic session gate behavior", which is right about loading but implies observation capture is guaranteed where hooks exist. It is not, anywhere: capture is an MCP tool call prompted by a rules file.

## Suggested shape

| Client | Persona loads automatically | Syncs automatically | Capture |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | hook | hook | tool call, prompted by rules file |
| everything else | tool call at agent discretion | manual or none | tool call, no prompt |

## Definition of done

- One vocabulary across README and page: persona, not fingerprint; no "memory layer".
- The havruta line survives, and ideally lands on the page too (T-063 item 8).
- One capability matrix, in the README, with the page's spec block derived from it.
- A check that fails when the two drift, or a comment at both ends pointing at the other.
title: Sync README with the landing page, and make the capability matrix one source
